newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sees lack of clarity in coffee market.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sees lack of clarity in coffee market.

text.p: A top Colombian coffee official, suggesting that commodity markets are about as transparent as a cup of expresso, said the official inventories of consumer countries fail to account for all the coffee that has been exported in the last year.

"There seems to have been a small increase (in inventories) according to the reports coming in from the United States and Europe," said John Naranjo, production manager of the National Coffee Growers' Federation.

"Japan has increased a little and Europe as well, and the United States a little bit. But these are very small numbers that don't explain the difference between what's being exported and what's being accumulated as green coffee," he said.

Naranjo did not specify how much coffee was actually unaccounted for. But he said world production is currently estimated at about 80 million 60-kg bags of coffee per year, while consumption was about 75 to 76 million bags. And the numbers, when factoring in consumer inventories, simply don't add up.

"If I look at the export numbers over the last few years, and then over the last 12 months ... and I confront that with any consumption figure then there has to have been an increase in inventories somewhere," he said.
"There's a fact here that isn't very clear," Naranjo said.

A report in Bogota's El Tiempo newspaper said major roasters may have secretly stockpiled as much as 4.5 million 60- kg bags of coffee over the last year in a bid to gain some leverage over producer countries.

Naranjo did not comment directly on the newspaper report, which he said he had not seen. But he stressed that inventories in consumer countries remained very low, historically, and were supportive of the recent sharp run-up in world prices.
"Inventories of certain types of coffee, such as the milds or arabicas, are practically non-existent," he told Reuters.
